headline: Guidance raised as growth broadens despite margin pressure
summary_short: Revenue rose 13% to €720M (15% in constant currency), with double-digit growth in every region. Reported net profit fell 15% to €110M on one-off refinancing and buyback charges, though adjusted EPS climbed 19% to €0.74.
summary_long: Fiscal Q3 revenue grew 13% reported (15% constant-currency) to €720M, led by DTC (+14%) outpacing B2B, with double-digit growth across Americas, EMEA and APAC. Gross margin fell 140bps to 59.1% on FX, U.S. tariffs and Australia-acquisition purchase accounting, partly offset by capacity absorption. Adjusted EBITDA rose 11% to €242M (margin -70bps to 33.7%) on the same drags. Reported net profit fell 15% to €110M on €22M of non-recurring refinancing/buyback charges; adjusted EPS rose 19% to €0.74. The company completed a €230M accelerated buyback, refinanced its senior notes, and ended the quarter with €694M cash and 1.8x net leverage. Birkenstock raised FY26 guidance for revenue growth (15% constant-currency) and Adjusted EBITDA (at least €710M).

drivers.explanation: Company raised FY26 revenue-growth and Adjusted EBITDA guidance, citing continued brand strength and DTC growth outpacing B2B.
DTC growth accelerated to 14% (16% cc), outpacing B2B's 13% (15% cc), driven by strength in both digital and in-store channels.

Unfavorable currency translation (60bps), incremental U.S. tariffs (70bps) and product mix, plus a 20bps mark-up tied to the Australia distributor acquisition, partly offset by improved capacity absorption.
Fell on unfavorable FX (60bps) and incremental U.S. tariffs (70bps), partly offset by improved capacity absorption.
Reduced by about €22M of non-recurring, non-cash charges tied to the accelerated share repurchase and senior-notes refinancing.
Adjusted net profit rose 15% while adjusted EPS rose 19%; the gap is explained by the reduced share count following the €230M buyback.
Rose on €900M of new senior notes issued, partly offset by the €428.5M repayment of the redeemed notes and the €230M accelerated buyback.
Higher year-over-year as the company continued investing in production capacity and retail expansion.

Note on period labeling: this shard labels the quarter ended June 30, 2026 as 'FY2026 Q2' (calendar quarter-end convention), but the company's own release calls it 'fiscal third quarter 2026' — Birkenstock's fiscal year ends September 30, so its fiscal Q1-Q4 run one quarter ahead of the calendar-quarter labels used across every event on this shard. This is a consistent, shard-wide offset, not unique to this filing. Note on currency: the entity registry tags 'currency: USD' (the NYSE ADS trading currency), but Birkenstock's financial statements are reported in EUR; all KPI values above are taken directly from the EX-99.1 press release in EUR, not converted. Reported EPS (€0.60) and Adjusted EPS (€0.74) are both diluted, same-basis y/y comparisons against the prior-year quarter's reported (€0.69) and adjusted (€0.62) figures per the release's own reconciliation tables — this is distinct from the shard's 'eps_usd' estimate/actual pair (Yahoo consensus €0.75275 vs Yahoo-tagged actual €0.74), which mixes sources and should not be used for surprise math this quarter.
